test_title: SSC CGL 2021 Tier-I (Held On : 21 April 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The Hindu Marriage Act was enacted in the year ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1955.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Hindu Marriage Act was enacted in the year 1955.**
 
• **Marriage Law Act:**
 
 
• The Hindu Marriage Act is an Act of the Parliament of India enacted in **1955**.
 
• According to Section 2 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, marriage in any form among Hindus, regardless of caste or creed or any person, is bound to abide by the rules of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
 
• The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 was intended to secure the rights of marriage for the bride and groom who are Hindus and are bound under the sacred bond of marriage under any ceremony.
 
• The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 removed any distinction under the law of marriage between a young woman and a widow and both are treated equally under this law.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Hindu marriage act applies to all over Indian states and the Union territories, Jammu and Kashmir being an exception to it.
 
• Marriage is directly registered by the Registrar of Marriage under **section 8** of the Hindu Marriage Act-1955 on the same working day.
 
• Verification of all the documents is carried out on the date of application and thereafter Marriage is registered on the same working day by the registrar of marriage appointed by the Govt. of India and a marriage certificate is issued.
 
• **Section 5** of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 makes a marriage lawful only if the groom has attained the age of 21 years at the time of marriage and the bride has attained the age of 18 years at the time of marriage.
 
• The couple should not be in a prohibited relationship unless their custom permits them to get married.
 
• The couple should not be sapindas (cousins) unless their custom permits them to get married.
